title: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say

reading.body:
This is a case of an automated alert being treated as an identification. A camera system supplied license plate information that led deputies to believe a car was a stolen Camaro tied to aggravated robberies, and that belief was carried into a felony stop with at least five patrol cars, a helicopter, drawn guns and handcuffs. The failure sits at the handoff between the system's output and the officers' decision to act on it, because the deputies could not read the plates themselves and proceeded anyway.

Catching it would have required the plate to be confirmed visually before the stop escalated, or the unreadable read to be treated as no match rather than a match. The reporting describes deputies calling for backup after failing to read the plates, which means the gap was visible at the scene before the men were handcuffed. A verification step at that point, rather than after, is what the sequence shows was missing.

What is not established is whether the camera system misread a plate or returned a false match, and the sheriff's office review of body worn camera video is a check on procedure, not a finding. The men's planned internal affairs complaint and the mother's plan to hire an attorney are allegations and intentions, not conclusions.

reports.title: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say

summary:
On Aug. 3 in Cypress, Harris County sheriff's deputies mistook two men, both 19 years old, Anthony and Julian, for car thieves. Deputies surrounded Anthony's Camaro with at least five patrol cars and a helicopter, pointed guns, handcuffed them, and Julian said a deputy threatened to shoot and kill him. The men had just returned from a gas station. Deputies thought the car was a stolen Camaro linked to aggravated robberies, based on Flock camera license plate information, but they could not read the plates and called for backup. After handcuffing the men, deputies realized it was the wrong car.

The men are not facing charges. Anthony's mother plans to hire an attorney and wants deputies held accountable. Both men plan to file a formal complaint with internal affairs. The sheriff's office says supervisors, including the district captain and shift lieutenants and sergeants, will review body worn camera video to check whether procedures and protocols were followed.
title_en: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say
